And news also reached Saladin
that the king of the Germans had departed and was coming by way of Constantinople with two hundred thousand horsemen and foot-soldiers.
And his heart was grieved,
and he sent Baha al-Din ibn Shaddad as an envoy
to the Caliph
and to all the kings of the East,
that they should come to their aid quickly,
otherwise the Islamic community would perish completely.
And when the year 1500 and... {OCR?} entered,
586 of the Arabs [1190 AD]:
while Saladin was resting, in that he had moved away from the camp of the Franks,
and the Franks had no other concern left except the siege against Acre,
then suddenly the army of the Franks attacked the camp of the Arabs.
And Saladin was out hunting,
but his brother al-Adil was prepared,
and he raised a war cry among the troops,
and they mounted.
And they mingled with one another,
and many fell from among the Arabs.
And if night had not overtaken them,
it would have been a complete defeat.
And the Franks withdrew and went to their camp.
And winter was near,
and there was terrible mud between the two camps,
and no one was able to ride a horse or to approach his adversary.
And news of Saladin was cut off from those who were in Acre,
and their news from him.
And by swimming, one of the Arabs who was inside escaped by way of the sea,
and he came to Saladin and reported
that the Franks were vigorously fighting against the city,
and that they had built high towers {OCR: wooden siege engines/towers} that looked inside the city,
and that those inside were enduring {OCR?} great distress.
Saladin mounted and went against the Franks,
so that they might be occupied with battle with him,
and those inside might have a little relief.
And he found that they had dug deep trenches around themselves,
and that no one was able to reach them.
Then Saladin bit his fingers [in regret/grief],
and he returned and camped on Tell al-Ijl (the Hill of the Calves),
at a great distance from the Franks.
And all the kings of the Arabs began to gather to him:
